props.text: Instead of filling a space, Sculptra prompts your skin to rebuild collagen. The change is gradual, which is exactly why people choose it.

Sculptra is made of poly-L-lactic acid, a material the body absorbs. It's placed in the deeper layers of the skin, where it prompts your own cells to make new collagen.
Because your body does the building, results arrive slowly over a few months. Most people need two or three sessions a few weeks apart. Once the series is done, the result can last two years or more.

Flattened cheeks regain some of their shape.

Filler adds volume the day it's placed. Sculptra prompts your body to make its own collagen, so the change builds over months and tends to last longer.
Why does it look full, then go down?
The fluid Sculptra is mixed with causes swelling for a day or two. Once that's absorbed, the collagen starts building in its place.
Is one session of Sculptra enough?
Usually not. Most people need two or three, a few weeks apart. Your provider will suggest a number at your consultation.
Why do I have to massage it?
Massage helps spread the product evenly under the skin. It lowers the chance of small lumps forming.

props.text: Every treatment at Westlake Medical Aesthetics is provided by our highly skilled medical providers.
Your first visit is a consultation with one of them. They'll look at what you'd like to change and recommend a plan that suits your skin and your schedule.
Experienced oral and maxillofacial surgeon serving Westlake and the greater DFW area

Dr. Stone is the visionary leader of Stone Surgical Arts, Stone Dental Implant Center and Westlake Medical Aesthetics. With unrivaled expertise, she's committed to artistic surgical excellence and patient well-being.
What is the difference between a day spa and a medical spa?

A day spa is about relaxation, with treatments like massages and basic facials. A medical spa offers treatments that change the skin itself, such as injectables, microneedling and chemical peels, and they're provided by licensed medical providers after a medical assessment.
Who will be performing my treatments?

Brooke, our nurse practitioner injector, does every injection. Abby, our medical aesthetician and senior laser technician, looks after facials and skin treatments. You'll know who is treating you before your appointment.

The treatments we offer are well established and, in trained hands, carry a low risk of side effects. We check your medical history first, go through the risks of your treatment at your consultation, and tell you if something isn't right for you.
What should I expect during my initial consultation?

We'll ask what you'd like to change, go through your medical history and look at your skin. You'll leave with a written plan and a quote. Your first consultation can be in person or by video, and whether you start that day is up to you.
Do treatments like Botox or filler hurt?
Most people describe a quick pinch. The needles are very fine, most fillers contain a local anesthetic, and we can apply numbing cream first if you'd like.
How long do the results of Botox and dermal fillers last?
Botox usually lasts three to four months. Dermal fillers last six to eighteen months, depending on the product and where it's placed.
Is there any downtime after a procedure?

Often none. You can go straight back to your day after Botox, a HydraFacial or dermaplaning. Fillers can leave some swelling or bruising for a few days, and Morpheus8 and deeper peels need a few days more. Each treatment's page lists its downtime.
How much do medical spa treatments cost?

It depends on the treatment and how much you need, so we quote at your consultation, before anything is done. Our membership is $149 a month and includes a monthly facial and 10% off treatments, and financing is available through Cherry and CareCredit.

props.text: About fifteen minutes, no anesthetic and no downtime. Placed by our nurse practitioner, who usually starts with fewer units than you'd expect.
Pricing depends on the number of units and the areas treated. You'll get a quote at your consultation.

Botox and Xeomin are both botulinum toxin type A, a purified protein that temporarily relaxes the muscle it's placed in. Small amounts in the upper face stop those muscles from creasing the skin, so the lines they cause soften.

It doesn't fill, tighten or remove anything. A line you can still see when your face is completely relaxed is etched into the skin, and Botox alone will only improve it slowly. That's the first thing your provider checks.
What it can do for you
Most people describe how they look rather than what they want done: tired, annoyed, older than they feel. In the upper face, that usually comes down to three muscles.
Forehead lines soften without dropping your brow.
The frown line between your eyebrows stops making you look cross.
Crow's feet ease when you smile.
A heavy brow can lift slightly when the muscle pulling it down relaxes.
Most healthy adults are good candidates. Your consultation is where we confirm that and work out how much you need. For a first treatment, it's usually less than you'd think.

You're pregnant or breastfeeding, have a neuromuscular condition, have an infection where you'd be treated, or your lines are static. In that last case, your provider may suggest a skin treatment or filler instead.

What happens when it wears off?
Your muscles gradually go back to how they worked before, and so do the lines. Nothing ends up worse than it was.

props.text: Non-invasive treatments that soften lines, restore volume and help your skin make more of its own collagen, so you look your best without surgery. Open any treatment to see how long it takes, when you'll see results and how long they last.

Neuromodulators soften the lines that come from movement, fillers restore volume, and biostimulators like Sculptra help your skin build its own collagen over time. Every injection is done by our nurse practitioner.

Botox and Xeomin relax the muscles that crease the skin, softening forehead lines, frown lines and crow's feet. Xeomin has no accessory proteins, which can help if Botox seems to wear off faster than it used to.
Two more neuromodulators that work the same way as Botox. Dysport spreads a little further, which can suit a larger area like the forehead, and Jeuveau is often chosen for frown lines.

Hyaluronic acid filler restores shape and volume to the lips, cheeks, chin and jawline, and can soften hollows under the eyes. Placement is planned around your facial structure so the result looks like you.
Sculptra is a biostimulator. Instead of filling a space, it prompts your skin to rebuild collagen, so results appear gradually over a few months and can last two years or more.

These treatments prompt your skin to repair and renew itself. Most are done as a short series, and results keep improving for a few months after the last session.

Radiofrequency energy delivered through fine microneedles tightens and smooths the deeper layers of the skin while leaving the surface largely intact. It works well on the jawline, the neck and acne scarring.

A peel lifts away damaged surface skin to even out tone, fade sun spots and refine texture. Light peels have almost no downtime, deeper ones need about a week, and we'll help you pick one that fits your schedule.

SkinPen creates thousands of tiny channels in the skin, which starts its natural repair process and boosts collagen. It's a good fit for acne scars, enlarged pores and early fine lines.

Regular facials keep skin clear, smooth and hydrated between treatments. Members get one every month as part of their plan.

Cleansing, exfoliation, extractions and hydration in a single treatment. We offer several versions, from 45 to 90 minutes, so your aesthetician can match the facial to your skin, and you can go straight back to your day.

Dermaplaning is a gentle exfoliation. Your aesthetician glides a sterile blade across the skin to lift away dead surface cells and fine facial hair, the peach fuzz, leaving skin smoother and brighter. Makeup and skincare go on more evenly afterward.

Boosters are targeted serums added to your HydraFacial, chosen for what your skin needs that day, whether that's brightening, firming or extra hydration. They're infused during the facial, so there's nothing extra to book.

A small amount of your blood is drawn and spun to concentrate the platelets, which are then returned to the skin. It's a good choice if you'd rather avoid fillers or synthetic products.

What is the difference between a day spa and a medical spa?

A day spa is about relaxation, with treatments like massages and basic facials. A medical spa offers treatments that change the skin itself, such as injectables, microneedling and chemical peels, and they're provided by licensed medical providers after a medical assessment.
Who will be performing my treatments?

Brooke, our nurse practitioner injector, does every injection. Abby, our medical aesthetician and senior laser technician, looks after facials and skin treatments. You'll know who is treating you before your appointment.

The treatments we offer are well established and, in trained hands, carry a low risk of side effects. We check your medical history first, go through the risks of your treatment at your consultation, and tell you if something isn't right for you.
What should I expect during my initial consultation?

We'll ask what you'd like to change, go through your medical history and look at your skin. You'll leave with a written plan and a quote. Your first consultation can be in person or by video, and whether you start that day is up to you.
Do treatments like Botox or filler hurt?
Most people describe a quick pinch. The needles are very fine, most fillers contain a local anesthetic, and we can apply numbing cream first if you'd like.
How long do the results of Botox and dermal fillers last?
Botox usually lasts three to four months. Dermal fillers last six to eighteen months, depending on the product and where it's placed.
Is there any downtime after a procedure?

Often none. You can go straight back to your day after Botox, a HydraFacial or dermaplaning. Fillers can leave some swelling or bruising for a few days, and Morpheus8 and deeper peels need a few days more. Each treatment's page lists its downtime.
How much do medical spa treatments cost?

It depends on the treatment and how much you need, so we quote at your consultation, before anything is done. Our membership is $149 a month and includes a monthly facial and 10% off treatments, and financing is available through Cherry and CareCredit.
